tip: The -iyor ending is the present continuous for what is happening now: bekliyorsunuz, you are waiting, lines up with şu anda, right now.
The -la ending means with and stacks after a possessive: arkadaş plus -ım (my) plus -la gives arkadaşımla, with my friend.
To say before doing something, put -madan önce on the verb: Uyumadan önce means before sleeping.
yüzünden means because of and is used for a cause you blame: rüzgâr yüzünden, because of the wind, points at what caused the delay.
The -se ending means if: giderseniz means if you go, setting up the condition for the rest of the sentence.
To say I need to do something, use the verb plus -mem gerekiyor: yenilemem gerekiyor means I need to renew.
Her ihtimale karşı is a fixed phrase meaning just in case, literally against every possibility.
The -arak ending means by or while doing: koşarak means by running, describing how I got home.
Plurals take -lar after back vowels and -ler after front ones: yumurtalar (eggs) but ekmekler (breads).
An infinitive plus için means in order to: almak için means in order to buy.
Turkish says şarkı söylemek, literally to say a song, for to sing: şarkı söyledi means sang.
Add -yle to a noun to say with that feeling: öfke (anger) plus -yle gives öfkeyle, angrily.
The -ce ending turns an adjective into an adverb: güzel (nice) becomes güzelce, nicely.
A specific, known object takes -i: haber becomes haberi, marking the news as a definite thing already in mind.
Both nouns get marked in this chain: zeytinyağlıların ends in -ın (of the dishes) and kralı adds -ı pointing back, so kralıdır means their king.
olmazsa olmazı is a set phrase for the indispensable part, literally if-it-isn't it-isn't, so cacığın olmazsa olmazı means the must-have of cacik.
birbiri means each other, and with -yle it becomes birbirleriyle, with one another.
Put en before an adjective for the superlative, the most: en sevdiğim means the one I love most.
The -çi ending names the person who does something: bek plus -çi gives Bekçi (guard), and ziyaret plus -çi gives ziyaretçiler, visitors.
-dan marks from and -ya marks to: İstanbul'dan Ankara'ya means from Istanbul to Ankara.
To report what someone would do, the verb becomes a noun: edeceğini means that he would do, the thing bildirdi (informed) reports.
The aorist -ar ending states timeless facts: doğar (rises) and batar (sets) tell what the sun always does.
Keşke means if only and pairs with a verb in -se: Keşke ... gidebilsek means I wish we could go.
The -meden ending means without doing: çay içmeden means without drinking tea.
Adding -ince to a verb means when or as soon as: Yaz gelince means when summer comes.
-ebilir added to a verb means can or could: gez plus -ebilir gives gezebilir, so gezebilir miyiz asks could we wander.
The -ip ending links two verbs done by one person: giyinip evden çıktım means got dressed and left the house, only the last verb fully conjugated.
The -mış ending marks something heard or inferred, not witnessed: varmış means there apparently was, and yapılmış, apparently built.
